name: @dezhouzhang/archery-query-mcp

tools.name: archery_query_readonly
tools.description: Main entry point for production database and business-data investigations, including SQL/table/schema queries, companyId, employee/staff records, attendance/payroll/workflow data, Cloud Stream consumer-fallback input rows, EVENT_TABLE output rows, and screenshots or bug reports describing incorrect application data. Prefer this over JumpServer when validating business records, even if the request says production, online, read-only, investigate, or names a cloud. Do not use for containers, pods, services, logs, host processes, remote commands, actual Kafka topic messages, Kafka broker lag, migrate, datafix, restart, or deployment. Every query must resolve and freeze one complete cloudName, instanceName, and dbName target. Unless the user explicitly asks to review or freeze SQL without executing it, call this first with bugContext, SQL, and optional maxRows. Pass companyId plus canonical businessGroupId when MCP must resolve that target, or provide an already trusted complete physical target directly. companyId is not an automatic SQL predicate. cloud_stream_event_table_input_v1 is a consumer fallback table. cloud_stream_event_table_output contains only sends that explicitly use com.ihr360.cloud.stream.core.EventSendMode#EVENT_TABLE; EventSendMode.MQ does not automatically appear there. Attendance input data, 阻塞, and 消息阻塞 mean input fallback rows and do not imply a status predicate. Use the separate Kafka Query MCP, not Archery, for actual Kafka messages, timestamps, partitions, offsets, keys, or values. Missing input/output rows do not prove that a Kafka message was not sent, delivered, or consumed. Safe low-risk reads execute in one call and return top-level status, rows, columns, and executionId; staged queries return a prepared query and nextAction=archery_execute_query.

tools.name: archery_prepare_query
tools.description: Prepare and freeze a production read-only SQL query without executing it. Infer and pass the canonical businessGroupId when the logical business is clear. Use this only when the user explicitly asks to review or freeze SQL without executing it. For every ordinary read-only query, call archery_query_readonly first and let MCP return a staged nextAction when required; do not pre-classify SQL by GROUP BY, JOIN, aggregation, ordering, or maxRows.

tools.name: archery_resolve_company_location
tools.description: Diagnostic/preflight only. Returns available company mappings but not an execution instruction. When instance matching is ambiguous, instanceCandidates contains the exact matched readable instance names for user confirmation. For normal production queries call archery_query_readonly first; do not copy returned mappings into physical scope fields.

tools.name: archery_resolve_company_by_account
tools.description: Resolve companyId from an exact auth-center accountName found in a ZenTao bug or other explicit user-provided evidence. This restricted tool uses dedicated credentials and a fixed physical target/table internally. Pass only the account value; do not use it for fuzzy search, ordinary company routing, or arbitrary SQL.

tools.name: archery_runtime_diagnostics
tools.description: Report this MCP process runtime and required environment visibility without exposing secrets

instructions:
This MCP server is for PRODUCTION ONLINE DATABASE AND BUSINESS-DATA READS ONLY.
Use it to query and validate SQL, tables, schemas, database rows, companyId, employee/staff records, attendance/payroll/workflow records, and application screenshots or bug reports that describe missing, incorrect, or inconsistent business data.
Prefer this MCP over JumpServer when the user asks whether a business record or database value is correct, even if the request also says production, online, read-only, investigate, 杭州云, 北京云, or 华为云.
Do not use it for host assets, Docker containers, Kubernetes pods/services/logs, processes, ports, files, remote shell commands, migrate, datafix, restart, or deployment; those are JumpServer/runtime operations.
Do not use it for test, development, local, SIT, UAT, staging, or other non-production data.
If the requested environment is non-production or unclear, do not call these tools; ask the user to confirm the environment or use the appropriate non-production data source.

Every query must resolve and freeze one complete physical target: cloudName, instanceName, and dbName. Identify the target in one of two ways: pass companyId plus the canonical businessGroupId so MCP resolves the complete target, or provide an already trusted complete cloudName, instanceName, and dbName directly. companyId is a routing input, not a universal execution field, and it never injects a companyId predicate into SQL.
Before calling, infer the logical business from the full user request, bug details, and current code context. When one business is clear, pass its canonical businessGroupId. When ambiguous, omit it; MCP fallback only uses strong SQL identifiers and otherwise asks for a choice.

After a successful query, reuse the returned canonical businessGroupId for follow-up queries unless the business domain changes.
If the user explicitly asks to review or freeze SQL without executing it, use archery_prepare_query. Otherwise, for every candidate single-statement read-only SQL query, call archery_query_readonly first and let MCP decide whether to execute it or return a staged nextAction. Do not choose archery_prepare_query because the SQL contains GROUP BY, JOIN, ordering, aggregation, or a larger bounded maxRows value.
Use archery_resolve_company_location only for diagnostics; its mappings are not an executable physical scope and must not be copied into cloudName, instanceName, or dbName.
When a ZenTao bug or the user explicitly provides an account and companyId is unknown, use archery_resolve_company_by_account. Pass the exact account only. The tool owns its fixed auth-center target and SQL; never guess or rewrite its table or fields.
Never guess an Archery instanceName, dbName, or company location. Select businessGroupId only from the recommended catalog when context is clear; omit it when ambiguous and let MCP fail closed.
Cloud Stream persistence tables are not Kafka topic message history. cloud_stream_event_table_input_v1 is a consumer fallback table, not a copy of every consumed message. cloud_stream_event_table_output contains only sends that explicitly use com.ihr360.cloud.stream.core.EventSendMode#EVENT_TABLE; EventSendMode.MQ and ordinary Kafka sends do not automatically appear there. For attendance, the business terms input data, 阻塞, and 消息阻塞 refer to input fallback rows and do not imply a status predicate. Bounded table browsing and GROUP BY topic or GROUP BY topic, companyId statistics use the trusted complete fixed target directly and do not require companyId as a routing input. When the user asks for actual Kafka topic messages, timestamps, partitions, offsets, keys, or values, do not use Archery; use the separate Kafka Query MCP when available. Missing input/output rows do not prove that a Kafka message was not sent, delivered, or consumed.
